lines.vo: Naming a feeling can turn down your brain's alarm.
That's not being dramatic. That's a brain trick.
So when the week gets heavy, Tasha writes one word in her Life Reset Planner: stressed.
Deep in your brain, the amygdala lights up when something feels threatening.
In a UCLA brain scan study, about thirty people looked at angry and scared faces.
When they picked a word for the feeling, the amygdala tended to quiet down more than when they just picked a name for the face.
Researchers call it affect labeling. It won't fix the problem, but it can take the edge off.
Name it, then plan it. That's how you stay calm and on track.
